### M3 — Trees (the collection)

**Outcome:** the owner can catalogue the whole collection with photos and a care journal.

#### T3.1 — Trees
- **Depends on:** T1.1, T2.2
- **Scope:** `Tree` per §4 (the species can be blank or pending — the tree page shows a
  "species being researched…" state). New/edit form with a species typeahead (T2.3's resolve
  flow, including "add a species"), area picker, style/size/stage enums with help text, design
  goals. Index: table on desktop / cards on mobile (UI rule), filters (garden, area, species,
  stage, health, status), sort. Tree page: header (primary photo, nickname, species, badges for
  stage/health/hardiness verdict), a derived "years in training" and "estimated age", and tabs
  (Overview · Journal · Photos · Tasks · Advisor — later tabs are placeholders). Status change
  flow (dead/sold/gifted with a reason) keeps the history; alive-only by default in lists.
  `number` (per-user sequence, "No. 047") and `tag_code` (`NBR-` + 4 unambiguous characters)
  generated on create; `location_detail` free text ("shelf 2").
- **Acceptance:** CRUD + filters covered by request/system specs; users can only see trees in
  gardens they can access.
- **Amended 2026-09-30 (T3.1 done):** `Tree` with `Tree::Numbering` (max + 1 under a user row lock; a deleted highest
  number can be reused), `Tree::TagCode` (`NBR-` + 4 from `23456789ABCDEFGHJKMNPQRSTUVWXYZ`, retried on collision),
  `MeasureInputs` (lengths in the user's unit, stored in cm), a decimal price with one app currency
  (`money.currency`, `format_money`), and `trees.user_id` as the collection owner (`Garden#collection_owner_for`),
  kept on moves. The species typeahead is a free-text combobox that resolves a typed name **on save** through
  `Tree::SpeciesChoice` after the tree validates, sharing the `species` rate limit with `/species/new` only when a
  lookup runs; ambiguous names come back as candidate cards with "None of these" in the same radio group, and a
  stale pick is unavailable even with a query. Garden and area are one grouped Location select. "Keeps the history"
  is read as *keeps the tree*: status is reversible and current-state only (no history table), and alive clears the
  date and reason. The tree page shows the verdict chip for living trees only (tree wiring pulled forward from T4.1),
  morphs live when a researched species becomes ready, goes two-column at `lg`, and disables the later tabs. The
  index has a "No living trees." state; `aria-sort` is on the `<th>`. Log care stays disabled, with copy from one
  query (`User#garden_access`), and "editor or above" has one definition (`GardenMembership::EDITOR_ROLES`,
  `.at_least`, `User#editable_gardens`). Fixes during review: one radio group for candidates, the Log care copy's
  extra layout query. Details in `docs/decisions.md` (T3.1 entries).

#### T3.2 — Photos & progression
- **Depends on:** T3.1
- **Scope:** multi-photo upload (desktop + phone camera `capture`) **through the app** (no direct
  uploads, the bucket stays private — §2), libvips variants (thumb, medium, large) **preprocessed in a
  background job** so viewing never waits, EXIF `DateTimeOriginal` → `taken_on` (fallback upload date,
  editable), angle tagging, primary photo. Photo timeline grouped by year. **Compare view:**
  pick two photos (defaults: earliest and latest front photos) → compare view per
  design-system §7.15 / §8.5 (always dark, accessible range input, side-by-side mode). **Align
  photos**: a simple editor that stores crop + scale/offset per photo so trunks line up.
  Content-type and size validation (≤ 25 MB, image/*, HEIC converted via vips if supported,
  otherwise documented).
- **Acceptance:** uploading a photo with EXIF sets the date; compare slider works in the system
  spec; variants are made by a background job, or on first request when missing.
- **Amended 2026-09-30 (T3.2 done):** `Photo` with its concerns (`Upload`, `Ordering`, `Primary`, `Aligning`,
  `Processing`) and the POROs `Photo::Exif`, `Photo::Alignment`, `Photo::Timeline`, `Photo::Comparison` and
  `Photo::Heic`. Upload is a full page (`/trees/:id/photos/new`) that sends one request per file, two at a time, with
  a `client_uuid` each; `create` is idempotent on it and answers a tile fragment (201/200), one sentence (422) or 429.
  The file is inspected from its header before it is attached (type, 25 MB, pixel and side limits, HEIC only when
  libvips decodes it). "Preprocessed in a background job" is one `PhotoProcessJob` per photo rather than
  `preprocessed: true`, with a `processing`/`ready`/`failed` state, a stalled rule and a live morph on the tree page
  and the Photos tab; the acceptance line above is reworded to match. Variants are 480, 960 and 2048 px JPEGs with
  EXIF stripped. The original is kept private and never served, and tree photos reach a browser only through
  `Trees::Photos::ImagesController` (garden members, private immutable cache); no Active Storage URL is emitted for
  one. The Photos tab is live (`?angle=front|all`, year rows, select two to compare), with a photo page (details,
  primary, delete). The tree hero shows the primary photo and a filmstrip, and the index card a thumbnail. Compare and
  the align editor are on a new `focus` layout. "A simple editor" became the full §7.25 editor: alignment is a scale
  and offsets as fractions of a shared 4:5 frame plus a crop, with onion skin and flicker, guides, a crop frame with
  handles and ratios, drag and pinch, a nudge pad, keys, an Align-to picker and an unsaved-changes confirm.
  `SpeciesPhoto` variant options are strings now. Thruster's upload limits are set in the compose file, and
  `nebari:smoke` checks HEIC decoding. Deferred: share, offline states, global shortcuts, AI badges, journal words on
  tiles, top-bar actions, desktop row thumbnails and an Align entry on the Photos tab. Details in `docs/decisions.md`
  (T3.2 entries).

#### T3.3 — Care journal
- **Depends on:** T3.1
- **Scope:** `CareEvent` with per-kind detail schemas (a `CareEvent::Details` PORO per kind:
  repotted → pot, soil mix text (links to inventory in M8), root reduction %; wired → wire
  material/gauge, branches; fertilized → product, NPK, dilution; treated → product, target,
  re-treat interval; moved → from/to area; protected → method). Log form that changes fields by
  kind (Stimulus), with optional photos attached. **Bulk log**: select several trees or a whole
  area → one event each. Journal timeline on the tree page merging events and photos. Side effects
  in model callbacks/methods: `repotted` updates `last_repotted_on`; `moved` updates
  `tree.area`; `wired`/`wire_removed` tracked for the follow-up rules.
- **Acceptance:** bulk log of "watered" across an area creates N events; per-kind validation;
  timeline ordering spec.
- **Amended 2026-10-06 (T3.3 done):** `care_events` per §4 plus `performed_on` (the event's date in the tree's zone,
  set only when `performed_at` changes, so a later garden move or zone edit doesn't move it to another day) and
  `batch_id`; `task_id` and `recorded_offline` exist with no behaviour yet. 17 kinds in `CareEvent::Vocabulary` (a
  past-tense title, a picker label and one of nine filter groups, Move & protect among them); the enum has no scopes or
  predicates (`protected` would shadow `Module#protected`). `CareEvent::Details` is a PORO per kind with inline errors
  under each field's own name; the protected method is `protection_method`, and a move's destination and an
  observation's health are create-only. Side effects in `CareEvent::SideEffects` under a tree lock: a repot keeps
  `last_repotted_on` on the latest repot (also after an edit or delete), the latest move moves the tree, and the latest
  observation that carries a health reading sets the tree's health; editing or deleting a move or a reading never
  changes the tree back. "Wired" is read from the latest of `wired`/`wire_removed` (`Tree#wired?`, `#wired_on`); no
  column. The log form is one kind per save, in the `modal` dialog from the tree hero (full page without Turbo), with a
  17-kind picker, the kind's fields, date and time in the tree's zone, notes and photos through the T3.2 uploader in
  an embedded mode (the photos join the tree as they upload and stay there if the form is abandoned). The kind can't
  change on edit; delete lives inside the edit dialog. The dialog skips broadcast refreshes while open and asks before
  discarding a touched form. **Bulk log** is its own page (`/care_batch/new`): one garden per batch, its living trees
  grouped by area with Select all, preselected from an area or the `/trees` filters; one transaction, one event per
  tree sharing a `batch_id`, shown as "Watered · bulk, 12 trees". The **Journal tab** (`/trees/:id/journal`) groups
  events and the day's unlinked photos by day with care-type chips in the URL and paging by 30 days
  (`CareEvent::Journal`, a constant number of queries a page); the Overview has a 4-row journal table, and the facts
  gain "Last repot" and "Last watered". Log care is enabled in the shell when the user can edit a garden with a living
  tree (`User#garden_access`), and on each area row and the `/trees` header. Not built (later tasks or deferred): the
  quick-log sheet, offline, pending markers, tasks and follow-ups, the garden-wide journal, CSV, "logged by",
  inventory pickers, bulk undo and bulk photos. Details in `docs/decisions.md` (T3.3 entries).

#### T3.3a — Phone bugs found after T3.2 (investigate and fix)
- **Depends on:** T3.2, T3.3 (added 2026-10-01 from the owner's report; seen on a phone only)
- **Where:** an iPhone, Chrome (WebKit, as every iOS browser is), on the deployed app.
- **Order:** bug 3 is fixed **before T3.3 starts**, on its own (`/zap:diagnose`, then `/zap:fix`), because T3.3's
  log, edit and delete dialogs are bottom sheets on a phone. Bugs 1 and 2 are this task, after T3.3.
- **Reported:**
  1. **A camera photo stays "Processing".** Add photo → Take photo → the upload finishes normally → the tile says
     "Processing" and never changes, but it can be opened and edited.
  2. **The align editor's overlay modes can't be changed.** On that photo, Onion / Flicker / Off: only Onion can be
     selected.
  3. **Bottom sheets can't be used.** Everything that opens as a bottom sheet (the native-looking menu that slides
     up) shows only a small part of itself, nothing in it responds, and the handle doesn't drag. True for every
     sheet met so far.
- **Leads from reading the code (none verified on a device):**
  - *Bug 1:* the owner saw it on the upload page only, and didn't check the Photos tab. The upload page has no
    stream by design (T3.2 R11), so a tile there stays "Processing" until the page is left: the likely fix is on
    that page (tiles that turn ready, or copy that doesn't read as stuck). First confirm on the Photos tab that the
    photo did become ready. If it didn't, look at `PhotoProcessJob` for a full-size camera original (memory in the
    container, an unrescued error, the job never running) and at why a stalled photo didn't turn to "failed" after
    `Photo::STALLED_AFTER`.
  - *Bug 2:* the mode radios sit in a disabled fieldset when the photo has no reference to align to, and a photo
    that isn't `ready` (or is the tree's only photo) has none. It may follow from bug 1. Either way a photo that is
    still processing shouldn't offer Align, and a disabled control should say why.
  - *Bug 3:* `Ui::OverlayHelper::DIALOG_PANEL_CLASSES` makes the sheet a flex column pinned to the bottom with
    `max-h-[90dvh]` and no height of its own. If the body part is `flex-1 min-h-0`, a browser that sizes the
    `<dialog>` to fit its content can give the body no height, which would leave only the handle and header
    showing. The handle is decorative (`aria-hidden`, swipe-to-close was deferred in T0.1), so it was never
    draggable; decide whether it should be. Cuprite runs Chrome at 390 px, so the specs don't see a Safari-only
    layout.
- **Scope:** reproduce each on the owner's phone (record the device, browser and whether it was the deployed app),
  find the cause, fix it, and add a regression spec where one can run in Cuprite. Where it can't (a Safari-only
  layout), add the check to the manual QA list in `docs/decisions.md`. Review every `components/dialog` call site
  at phone width, including the T3.3 log, edit and delete dialogs.
- **Acceptance:** on the owner's phone, a camera photo becomes ready on the Photos tab without a manual reload; a
  processing photo offers no Align; the overlay modes switch on a photo that has a reference; every sheet opens
  fully, scrolls and responds to taps.
- **Amended 2026-10-06 (T3.3a done in code; phone check pending for bugs 1–2):** bug 3 was fixed by `55d4bfb`
  (`flex-auto` body, `preventScroll`) and the owner confirmed it on the iPhone. Bug 1: the photo was ready on the
  server, but the upload page and the log form's uploader had no stream. `Photo::Processing` now broadcasts a replace
  of the upload tile to `[tree, :photo_uploads]`, both screens subscribe, `upload_controller.js` holds a replace that
  arrives before its tile, and `photos_resync` refreshes the tree page, Photos tab and Journal once after the photos
  stream reconnects. No polling. The production cable upgrades through Caddy (check with `curl --http1.1`). Bug 2:
  no WebKit fault was found; the overlay modes are disabled when the photo has no other ready photo, and the editor
  now says so ("Add another photo of this tree to use the overlay."). Align stays absent for a processing or failed
  photo. Bugs 1 and 2 wait for the manual phone check in `docs/decisions.md` (T3.3a entries).

#### T3.4 — Identify species from a photo (AI)
- **Depends on:** T3.1, T2.3
- **Scope:** on new tree ("Not sure what it is? Identify from photos"), upload 1–4 photos →
  `SpeciesIdentification` via a vision structured call: top 3 candidates with confidence and
  distinguishing features to check ("look for three-lobed leaves"), plus "insufficient
  information — photograph X". Picking a candidate runs the resolve flow. Ledgered + rate-limited.
- **Acceptance:** fixture-driven spec; low confidence shows guidance rather than a pick.
- **Amended 2026-10-06 (T3.4 done in code; phone check and cost measurement pending):** the entry is the tree form,
  new and edit: the species combobox's footer row and a link under the field, both "Not sure? Identify from a photo"
  (the design system's wording). They open a dialog in the `modal` frame over the form; a direct visit is a full
  page. `new` saves nothing: the page gets an id and the first upload creates the `SpeciesIdentification`, one request
  per file (1–4 photos, the tree photo rules from `Photo::UploadRules`, 60 uploads an hour). Only a stripped JPEG of
  at most 1568 px is stored per photo (`SpeciesIdentificationPhoto`), served only by
  `SpeciesIdentifications::ImagesController`. Identify starts `SpeciesIdentificationJob` (20 analyses a day a user;
  over the month's budget the start is refused with a 422 and the warning): one `species_identify` structured call,
  validated again by `SpeciesIdentification::Result`, with the result sent as a Turbo Stream replace of the state
  frame and reloaded when the stream (re)connects. No polling. A failure or a run stalled for 5 minutes shows Retry
  with the same photos. A result is pickable when the outcome is `identified` and the top confidence is at least
  `MIN_PICK_CONFIDENCE` (50); otherwise it shows guidance and "Possibly: …" as plain text. A pick runs
  `Species.resolve` by name, stores `chosen_species` and fills the form's species field; the tree changes on save.
  It counts toward the shared `species` limit (10 an hour) only when the catalogue has no exact match. Names are
  species-level. Model, job and request specs run on recorded fixtures, and
  `spec/system/species_identification_spec.rb` drives the dialog. Left out: an entry on the tree page, copying photos
  to the tree, the "Identified" tile badge, a history, resuming a draft and a cleanup job. The cost in
  `docs/ai-costs.md` is an estimate and unmeasured; the phone check, the `ai:smoke` run and the first 5 ledger rows
  are the owner's (the T3.4 entries in `docs/decisions.md`).

#### T3.5 — Quick log & offline sync
- **Depends on:** T3.2, T3.3
- **Already in place (T3.2):** `POST /trees/:tree_id/photos` takes one photo per request (multipart, `photo[image]`,
  `photo[angle]`, `photo[client_uuid]`) and is idempotent on `client_uuid` (201 created, 200 for a repeat on the same
  tree), so the `photo` operation posts to it as it is. The `photo_alignment` operation posts to the alignment
  `update` (`PATCH /trees/:tree_id/photos/:photo_id/alignment`), which stores the same normalised JSON for the same
  input. The offline "Not synced" tile state and the offline alignment save are this task's.
- **Already in place (T3.3):** `POST /trees/:tree_id/care_events` (editor or above, form params under `care_event`,
  `performed_at` accepted as ISO 8601 alongside the form's `performed_date`/`performed_time`) is idempotent on
  `care_event[client_uuid]`: a uuid already stored on the same tree creates nothing and answers 303 to the stored
  event with "Already logged."; one stored on another tree is a 422 ("This entry couldn't be saved. Open the form
  again."); a malformed or missing uuid is replaced server-side. It answers HTML only (no JSON yet; this task adds what
  its queue needs). `photo_client_uuids[]` links photos already uploaded to the tree, so the queue can post photos
  first and the event after, as the log form's embedded uploader does. `CareEvent::Batch` (`POST /care_batch`) logs
  one event per tree in one transaction with a shared `batch_id`, and a repeated `batch_id` is "Already logged." —
  the "Also log for N more" path can build on it. `recorded_offline` exists with no behaviour, and the journal entry
  component has no `sync_state` yet.
- **Goal:** logging care at the bench takes two taps and works without signal.
- **Scope:**
  - **Quick-log sheet** exactly per design-system §8.3: opened by the centre Log button (tree
    picker first when not on a tree page) or with a tree pre-filled; multi-select care-type
    toggles; up to 2–3 optional contextual fields; "When" defaulting to now; "Also log for N more
    on <location>"; sticky "Save · <type>" footer. Desktop: the sidebar "Log care" button and the
    `L` shortcut open it as a modal.
  - **Service worker** (Rails PWA `service-worker.js`): caches the app shell, fonts, icons and
    the Stimulus bundle; the user's tree list for the picker comes from a small Jbuilder JSON
    endpoint that's cached and refreshed on each online visit.
  - **Offline queue** — one general queue (`app/javascript/offline/`) with typed operations so
    later tasks can plug in: `care_event`, `photo` (this task), `task_completion` /
    `task_snooze` / `task_skip` (registered in T4.2) and `photo_alignment` (registered here, since
    T3.2 is done). Every operation carries a `client_uuid`. When offline (or the request fails on
    the network), the Stimulus controller stores the log — and any photos as blobs — in IndexedDB with a `client_uuid` and
    the local timestamp, shows the toast "Saved offline · will sync", and marks the tree page
    with a pending badge. Sync runs on the `online` event, on app open and via Background Sync
    where supported (iOS Safari has none — don't rely on it). Photos upload to the app first (a
    normal multipart POST, not a direct upload), then the event is posted.
  - **Server side**: creating a `CareEvent` or `Photo` with an existing `client_uuid` returns the
    existing record (idempotent); `performed_at` comes from the client; events are append-only,
    so there are no merge conflicts. If the tree was deleted or access was revoked in the meantime,
    the item fails with a visible "Couldn't sync 1 log" notice that keeps the data for export.
  - UI per design-system §7.22: sync indicator (all states) + "Sync now", sync sheet/popover,
    toasts, pending markers on journal entries/photo tiles/task rows, offline notice in the
    quick-log sheet, online-only panels, and the service-worker offline fallback page.
  - **"Keep a copy"** on a failed item moves it to an **unsynced archive** kept on the phone.
    Archived logs can be re-attached to another tree (then they sync normally) or exported as
    JSON/CSV. Discard removes the item (toast with Undo).
  - Settings › **Offline & sync** page: pending items, the archive, storage used on this device,
    "Sync now".
  - Document storage limits (browsers can evict IndexedDB; iOS home-screen apps get their own
    storage) in `docs/decisions.md`.
- **Acceptance:** system spec with Cuprite network emulation: go offline → log water for a tree
  with a photo → go online → exactly one event and one photo exist, even if sync runs twice;
  a server-rejected item (tree deleted) shows the reason and can be kept (archived, then
  re-attached) or discarded;
  a duplicate `client_uuid` POST returns 200 with the existing record; watering log is 2 taps
  after opening the sheet on a tree.
- **Amended 2026-10-07 (T3.5 done in code; phone check pending):** the two "Already in place" notes above describe
  the app before this task. The quick log is one sheet, rendered for nobody and filled on the phone: in a dialog from
  the centre Log button, the sidebar's Log care, `L`, the tree hero, the Journal tab and the Overview's journal table,
  and as the public page `/quick_log`. Eight care types (Photo logs no entry), two optional fields for Fertilise,
  Wire, Repot and Treat, shared Notes, When in the tree's zone, photos from the camera and "Also log for N more"
  (one operation per tree under one `batch_id`, not `CareEvent::Batch`). "More detail" opens the T3.3 log form, which
  stays the only place an entry is edited; the area rows and the `/trees` header keep the bulk page. **Every save
  goes through the offline queue and then syncs at once**, not only a save made offline, so there is one save path.
  The queue is `app/javascript/offline/` (IndexedDB, typed operations `care_event`, `photo` and `photo_alignment`,
  one `outcome` map): no answer, a 5xx, a 401 and a 429 leave operations waiting; a 404 or a 422 marks one failed with
  a reason. It is per user: a pass asks `GET /session.json` who is signed in and sends only that user's operations,
  and signed-out JSON requests get 401 with no redirect. The care entry, photo and alignment controllers answer JSON
  beside their unchanged HTML (a repeated `client_uuid` is a 200 with the stored record; for JSON only, `batch_id`
  and `recorded_offline` are accepted, a malformed uuid is refused and a future time is clamped). Care entry creates
  are limited to 1,000 an hour. The service worker (`/service-worker`, built from `Offline::Precache`) stores the
  assets and three public, user-neutral shells (`/quick_log`, `/offline/sync`, `/offline`) at install with no
  cookies, and answers any other failed or slow navigation (4 s) with the fallback page; it caches no private page,
  JSON or photo. The tree list comes from `/offline/trees.json` and is kept per user on the phone. **No Background
  Sync**: a sync runs on load, `pageshow`, when the tab becomes visible, on `online`, from "Sync now" and after a
  save. Built from §7.22: the sync indicator and sheet, the toasts, pending markers on the tree hero, Journal tab,
  Overview table and Photos tab, the offline notice, the fallback page, "Keep a copy" into the unsynced archive,
  re-attach, Discard with Undo, JSON and CSV export, and Settings › Offline & sync with storage figures. Upload tiles,
  the align editor's Save and the species combobox have offline states. `spec/system/quick_log_offline_spec.rb` is
  the acceptance spec. Left out: the inventory typeahead (M8), "Scan tag" and `/t/:tag_code` (T7.3), the wire
  follow-up, task auto-complete and the task operations (T4.2), pending markers on task rows (T4.2), species "Save
  as", the `?` overlay and other shortcuts, the desktop popover, a use of the online-only panel on a real screen,
  offline caching of visited pages, a zip export and a deleted-tree record (the 404 reason is one sentence for a
  deleted tree and for lost access). Opening the app with no signal and every iOS behaviour are unproven: Cuprite
  can't cut the service worker's own fetches. The decisions, the storage limits, the known gaps and the owner's
  phone check are the T3.5 entries in `docs/decisions.md`.

### M4 — Care Engine & Tasks

**Outcome:** the app tells each user what to do, when, and why — adjusted for their climate.

#### T4.1 — Season anchors & localised calendar
- **Depends on:** T1.3, T2.2
- **Scope:** implement §5.3 (`Anchors::Calculator`, constants file), `SeasonAnchorSet` computed
  per garden per season year (southern hemisphere season year = the July-to-June span, documented),
  `PhenologyObservation` logging UI ("I saw bud swell today" from the garden page or the journal)
  with overrides applied, and `CareCalendar.windows_for(species, garden)` (window `kind` best/possible and anchor
  uncertainty included). The care window bar component (design-system §7.18). Connect to the T2.5
  species page calendar. `Hardiness.verdict` (§5.2) with specs.
  **Amended 2026-09-30:** `Hardiness.verdict` landed in T2.5; T4.1 adds the cross-garden specs and tree/area wiring,
  and replaces the calendar text rows with dated bars.
- **Acceptance:** table-driven specs for anchors in Denver (6b), Brisbane (10b, southern,
  frost-free), Oslo (6a-ish, short season), Phoenix (9b, hot); an observation moves all dependent
  windows; verdict specs for maple/ficus/juniper across those gardens.
- **Amended 2026-10-08 (T4.1 done):** the engine is `app/models/anchors/` (`Anchors::Calculator.for(climate,
  season_year)` → an `Anchors::Set` of 13 anchors, each with a date or a reason it has none, a ± in days and a
  source; every heuristic in `Anchors::Offsets`). The ± is half the interquartile range of the yearly frost dates,
  shown in whole weeks. A season year's winter solstice is the one that opens it. `Garden#season_anchors(season_year)`
  returns the set with season observations applied and never writes; `SeasonAnchorSet` rows are written by
  `Garden#store_season_anchors!` after a climate or observation change, so they exist for the current season year ± 1
  **once a trigger has run**, and a garden computed before T4.1 has none until then (reads are computed in memory).
  `PhenologyObservation` is called a **season observation** in the UI: six observable anchors, one per garden, season
  year and anchor, replaced through `create`, logged by editors and owners from the garden page's new Season card or a
  link on the tree Journal tab; an observed bud swell or autumn colour carries the later anchor of its phase with it,
  and an observed frost moves only itself. `CareCalendar.windows_for(species, garden, season_year:)` returns dated
  `CareCalendar::Window`s (kind, anchor source, ±, or a missing reason) from `Species#effective_care_windows`. The
  species page calendar is now `components/care_calendar`: `components/window_bar` rows on a Jan–Dec axis with a
  status in words, the bracket and "≈ date ± n wk" text on an estimated start, a next-action sentence, a collapsed
  "Window details" list, and Reference mode in grey with no status or ±. Brisbane, Oslo and Phoenix have recorded
  ERA5 fixtures (`script/fixtures/record_era5`). **The fixtures don't match the labels above:** Denver is 5a,
  Brisbane 11a, Oslo 6b with a *longer* frost-free season than Denver's, and Phoenix 9b but not frost-free; the specs
  assert what ERA5 computes. **Moved to T4.2:** the stage filter and the other tree rules of §5.4, and the care
  windows panel on the tree page. Not built: any task, alert or dashboard, and an offline operation for season
  observations. The verdict specs found one rule to revisit (a dormancy-requiring species reads "hardy" in a heated
  indoor area where the outdoor chill is enough); no rule was changed. The decisions and known gaps are the T4.1
  entries in `docs/decisions.md`.

#### T4.2 — Task generation & task UI
- **Amended 2026-10-09: split in two.** **T4.2a** (the task engine) is done; the remainder is **T4.2b** (the task
  UI, actions, manual tasks and offline), done in code on 2026-10-10. Both follow this entry, which is kept as the
  original scope.
- **Depends on:** T4.1, T3.3, T3.5
- **Scope:** `Task` per §4 and `CarePlanningJob` implementing §5.4 (seasonal + follow-up rules,
  dedupe, updates when anchors move, expiry). Nightly schedule + run on relevant events (a tree
  created/stage changed, an event logged). Every task stores a human `reason`. Task actions as
  **resources, not custom actions** (per `.claude/rules/crud.md`): `POST /tasks/:id/completion`,
  `POST /tasks/:id/skip`, `POST /tasks/:id/snooze`, with undo as the matching `DELETE`. Done
  opens a pre-filled quick-log sheet; saving marks the task done. **Logging care auto-completes
  a matching open task** (same tree, activity maps to the event kind, window open). Task row
  component per design-system §7.16, including swipe gestures and the "why this task" expansion.
  Register the task operations with the T3.5 offline queue (done/snooze/skip work offline and show
  "Done 07:52 · not synced"). Manual tasks (one-off or simple recurrence: every N days).
  Tasks tab on the tree page; garden-level task list grouped Overdue / Today / This week / Upcoming
  windows.
- **Already in place (T3.3):** `care_events.task_id` (indexed, no foreign key) exists with no behaviour, and nothing
  runs after an event is logged: the auto-complete and planning hooks are this task's. Follow-up rules can read
  `Tree#last_repotted_on`, `Tree#wired?` / `#wired_on` and `Tree#last_watered_at`.
- **Already in place (T4.1):** `Garden#season_anchors(season_year)` (an `Anchors::Set`, nil while the climate isn't
  computed) and `CareCalendar.windows_for(species, garden, season_year:)` are the hooks: each `CareCalendar::Window`
  has `starts_on`/`ends_on` (nil with a `missing` reason), `kind`, `stages`, `priority`, `anchor_source` and
  `uncertainty_days`. Nothing filters by a tree's stage yet, and no other tree rule exists: both are this task's.
  `SeasonAnchorSet` rows exist for the current season year ± 1 once a trigger has run, and nothing rolls them forward
  when a season year turns over, so the nightly job should call `Garden#store_season_anchors!` or read through
  `season_anchors`. That method already runs after every season observation and climate change, which is where
  "moving an anchor updates open tasks' windows" can hook in. `components/window_bar` and `WindowBar::Axis.rolling`
  are ready for the tree page's care windows panel.
- **Acceptance:** specs for each rule in §5.4 (repot interval, health deferral, fertiliser pause
  after repot, wire-check chain until removed); running the job twice creates nothing new; moving
  an anchor updates open tasks' windows.

#### T4.2a — The task engine
- **Depends on:** T4.1, T3.3
- **Done 2026-10-09.** No route, controller, view, JavaScript or gem changed: nothing in the app shows a task yet.
- **Delivered:**
  - `Task` and the `tasks` table (§4), with `Task::Vocabulary` (sources, statuses, the 16 seasonal activities, the
    five follow-ups and a verb-first title for each), the scopes `actionable`, `acted_on`, `generated`, `seasonal`,
    `follow_ups` and `due_order`, and the state changes in the model: `complete!`, `skip!`, `snooze!` and `reopen!`
    (the undo of all three), with expiry and the snooze limits.
  - `CarePlan` (`app/models/care_plan/`): seasonal proposals with the §5.4 tree rules (stage filter, repot
    interval, health deferral, fertiliser pause, winter tasks by hardiness verdict, window conditions against the
    forecast), follow-up proposals (wire-check chain, repot aftercare, resume fertilising, back-budding check,
    re-treat), a reason for each, and `setbacks` for the windows that are deferred or withheld. Pure Ruby; every
    heuristic is in `CarePlan::Rules`.
  - `Tree#plan_care!` and `Garden#plan_care!`, which create, re-date, expire and withdraw tasks to match the plan
    and write nothing when nothing changed.
  - Auto-complete: a care entry completes the matching task (`Task.completed_by`, `care_events.task_id`), and
    deleting the entry reopens it.
  - `CarePlanningJob`: hourly (`every hour at minute 20`) and after the changes listed in §5.4's amendment. The
    garden run also stores the season anchor sets a new season year has left missing.
  - `bin/rails care:plan [GARDEN=<id> | TREE=<id>]`, which plans inline and prints each tree's tasks, reasons and
    setbacks.
  - `CareCalendar::Window` gained `conditions` and `rank`.
- **Acceptance met:** a spec for each §5.4 rule (`spec/models/care_plan/`), running twice creates and writes
  nothing, and moving an anchor updates open tasks' windows, due dates and reasons
  (`spec/models/tree/planning_spec.rb`). `spec/models/care_planning_acceptance_spec.rb` takes the seeded Japanese
  maple through a season year in the Denver fixture.
- **Not built:** everything in T4.2b; the health-drop diagnosis prompt (T5.1); weather and AI tasks. The decisions,
  departures and known gaps are the T4.2a entries in `docs/decisions.md`.

#### T4.2b — Task UI, actions, manual tasks & offline
- **Depends on:** T4.2a, T3.5
- **Scope:** Task actions as **resources, not custom actions** (per `.claude/rules/crud.md`):
  `POST /tasks/:id/completion`, `POST /tasks/:id/skip`, `POST /tasks/:id/snooze`, with undo as the matching
  `DELETE`. Done opens a pre-filled quick-log sheet; saving marks the task done. Task row component per
  design-system §7.16, including swipe gestures and the "why this task" expansion. Register the task operations
  with the T3.5 offline queue (done/snooze/skip work offline and show "Done 07:52 · not synced"). Manual tasks
  (one-off or simple recurrence: every N days). Tasks tab on the tree page, with the Overview's "Next up" and its
  care windows panel (the deferred and withheld windows with their reasons); garden-level task list grouped
  Overdue / Today / This week / Upcoming windows. Live updates when a task changes.
- **Already in place (T4.2a):** the rows exist and are kept right by `CarePlanningJob`. Read them through
  `tree.tasks` / `garden.tasks` with `actionable` and `due_order`; each has `title`, `reason` and `details` (a
  window condition's figures are there in °C, to format in the reader's units). Each resource calls one of
  `Task#complete!`, `#skip!`, `#snooze!` (false with an error on `:snoozed_until` for a date it refuses) and
  `#reopen!`. Saving a care entry already completes its matching task, so the quick log needs no task id for that.
  `CarePlan.new(tree).setbacks` feeds the care windows panel, with `components/window_bar` and
  `WindowBar::Axis.rolling` from T4.1. Nothing broadcasts when a task changes: this task chooses the streams. The
  `source` enum already has `manual`, with no rules for it: validation, expiry, snooze limits and recurrence for a
  manual task are this task's. The tree page's Tasks tab is still disabled and `TreesHelper::NEXT_UP_EMPTY` is the
  placeholder to replace.
- **Acceptance:** a system spec that completes, skips and snoozes a task and undoes each; Done through the quick
  log completes the task; the three operations sync from the offline queue; a manual task with a recurrence
  produces its next occurrence; the lists handle the empty state.
- **Done in code 2026-10-10.** The owner's phone check is pending (the last T4.2b entry in `docs/decisions.md`).
  The scope and "Already in place" paragraphs above are kept as written before the build.
- **Delivered:**
  - The three state resources under `/tasks/:task_id` (`completion`, `skip`, `snooze`; POST acts, DELETE undoes),
    for editors and above, answering HTML and JSON.
  - `components/task_row` (design-system §7.16) with `tasks/_list` and `tasks/_snooze_button`: the states, "why
    this task", the snooze menu and sheet, swipe (`swipe_task_controller.js`) and `/design` samples.
  - Row actions through the offline queue: `task_row_controller.js` writes a `task_completion`, `task_skip` or
    `task_snooze` operation and syncs at once, with toasts and Undo; `task_list_controller.js` draws what still
    waits ("Done 07:52" with the "Not synced" marker) and what failed.
  - Done through the quick log for the tasks one of its care types logs, with the entry carrying `task_id` so it
    completes exactly that task (§4's `CareEvent` note); one tap for the rest, with "Log details" in the toast when
    a care entry kind fits.
  - Manual tasks (`Task::Manual`, `TasksController`: add, edit, delete, for one tree) and repeating tasks
    (`Task::Repeating`: the next occurrence is created when this one is done or skipped, N days after that day).
    Migration: `tasks.title` and `tasks.repeat_every_days`.
  - The tree page: the Tasks tab (`/trees/:tree_id/tasks`: To do, Snoozed, Earlier), "Next up" and the care windows
    panel (`Tree::CareWindowsPanel`) on the Overview.
  - The garden: `/gardens/:garden_id/tasks`, grouped Overdue / Today / This week / Open now / Upcoming, then
    Snoozed (`Task::Agenda`, `Task::GardenList`), and a Tasks section on the garden page.
  - Live updates: page refreshes on `[tree, :tasks]` and `[garden, :tasks]` (`Task::Broadcasting`), from a keeper's
    change and from a `CarePlanningJob` run that changed something.
- **Acceptance met:** `spec/system/tasks_spec.rb` (complete, skip and snooze with their undos; Done through the
  quick log; a repeating task's next occurrence; the empty states; the garden's groups) and
  `spec/system/tasks_offline_spec.rb` (the three operations made with no signal and synced exactly once).
- **Departs from the scope above:** the garden list has two more groups than PLAN named (Open now, Snoozed) and its
  last heading reads "Upcoming"; a manual task is for one tree, never a whole garden; a repeating task counts from
  the day it was answered, not from its due date; the quick log does carry a task id.
- **Not built:** bulk task rows, the `D`/`S` shortcuts, tree thumbs on rows and the "remove follow-up" offer (left
  out of the design system's §7.16); garden-wide tasks; offline add, edit or delete of a manual task; a shell
  navigation entry for tasks; weather and AI tasks (T4.3, T5.1); the dashboard, month calendar and ICS feed (T4.4).
  The decisions, departures, what later tasks start from and the known gaps are the T4.2b entries in
  `docs/decisions.md`.

#### T4.3 — Weather alerts
- **Depends on:** T4.1, T1.4, T3.1
- **Scope:** `WeatherAlertsJob` implementing §5.5 after each forecast refresh (frost/heat
  thresholds: garden override → user setting → default); `WeatherAlert`
  records with affected trees; alert banners on dashboard/garden page; acknowledge; tasks with
  `source: weather` ("Move 4 trees on South bench into the garage before Thu night: forecast
  −6 °C").
- **Amended 2026-10-09 (T4.2a):** a care window's `conditions` (`min_night_temp_c`, `max_day_temp_c`) are already
  checked against the forecast by the planner (`CarePlan::Conditions`) and aren't this task's. `Task` exists, with
  `weather` in its `source` enum and no rules for that source yet: a weather task's dedupe key, expiry and what
  withdraws it are this task's to define. `CarePlanningJob` only touches `seasonal` and `follow_up` tasks
  (`Task.generated`), so it leaves weather tasks alone.
- **Acceptance:** fixture forecasts produce the expected alerts per exposure type; repeated runs
  dedupe; heated-indoor areas never alert on frost.

#### T4.4 — Dashboard & calendar
- **Depends on:** T4.2b, T4.3
- **Scope:** home dashboard (per UI rules' dashboard pattern): stats row (trees, tasks due,
  alerts, species), weather strip for the default garden, active alerts, Today / This week tasks,
  "windows opening soon", recent journal activity — laid out per design-system §8.1. Month
  calendar view of task windows per garden. A garden-wide **Journal** page per design-system §8.7
  (filters in the URL, day groups, timeline/table views, "This period" summary, CSV export). Keyboard shortcuts (design-system §6.4) with a `?` overlay.
  **ICS feed** per user with a secret token URL (tasks + windows) for subscribing in
  Apple/Google calendars. HTTP caching (`fresh_when`) on the dashboard.
- **Already in place (T4.2b):** tasks have their screens on the tree page and at `/gardens/:garden_id/tasks`, so
  the dashboard lists them rather than inventing a row. `Task::Agenda.new(tasks, today:)` already groups a relation
  or an array into `overdue`, `today`, `this_week`, `open_now`, `upcoming` and `snoozed`, with `due_count`,
  `overdue_count` and `first(n)`: the Today / This week lists and the "tasks due" stat are these. It takes one
  `today`, and `Task::GardenList` is per garden, so a dashboard across gardens in different zones must choose.
  Render rows with `tasks/_list` (`show_tree: true`); a page that lists tasks subscribes to `[garden, :tasks]` or
  `[tree, :tasks]` for refreshes. The care windows panel (`Tree::CareWindowsPanel`) is per tree; "windows opening
  soon" for a garden has no model yet. Not built and this task's: the `D`/`S` task shortcuts and the `?` overlay
  (only `L` exists, from T3.5), the month calendar, the ICS feed, and any shell navigation entry for tasks.
- **Already in place (T3.3):** `CareEvent::Journal` (day groups of events and unlinked photos, care-type groups,
  paging by whole days, `batch_size`) is per tree; the garden-wide page needs a garden-scoped version of it. The
  journal components (`components/journal_entry` in its full, compact and row variants, `journal_day`, the care-type
  `toggle_chip` row) have no `show_tree` local yet. `batch_id` groups a bulk save (for "Show trees"), and the tree's
  Journal tab is the per-tree view to link to.
- **Acceptance:** system spec for a seeded garden; the ICS feed validates (icalendar gem) and
  rejects bad tokens.

### M5 — AI Care Assistant

**Outcome:** Claude diagnoses problems and answers questions about a specific tree using its full context.

#### T5.1 — Health diagnosis from photos
- **Depends on:** T3.2, T3.3, T4.1
- **Scope:** "Something's wrong" flow on the tree page: 1–5 photos + an optional symptom
  description → `HealthAssessment` via `tree.diagnose_later`. Context snapshot: species profile
  (pests/diseases, watering, hardiness), garden climate + last 14 days of weather + forecast,
  season anchor ("3 weeks after leaf-out"), last 90 days of journal, stage, area exposure.
  Structured result: `likely_causes[]` {cause, category (pest/disease/watering/nutrient/
  environmental/physical/normal_seasonal), likelihood, evidence_from_photos, evidence_from_history},
  `urgency` (`monitor`/`soon`/`urgent`), `immediate_actions[]`, `avoid[]`,
  `follow_up_in_days`, `questions_to_confirm[]`, and "possibly normal" handling (e.g. autumn
  colour, inner needle shedding). Result page with one-click "create tasks from actions" and
  "log as observation"; `health` suggestion update requires confirmation. Result arrives via Turbo
  Stream.
- **Amended 2026-10-09 (T4.2a):** §5.4's last follow-up, the prompt to run a diagnosis after an `observation` entry
  lowers a tree's health, was left out of T4.2a because there was nothing to prompt for. It is this task's.
  `Task::Vocabulary::FOLLOW_UPS` has no entry for it yet, and tasks created from a result use `source: ai`, which
  has no rules yet either. While a tree is struggling or critical the planner already defers its repot, structural
  prune and defoliation (`CarePlan#setbacks`).
- **Acceptance:** fixture spec asserts the context builder includes weather + recent events; the
  task-creation mapping works; results are ledgered.

#### T5.2 — Per-tree advisor chat
- **Depends on:** T5.1
- **Scope:** `Conversation`/`Message` on the tree's Advisor tab. The context builder reuses T5.1's
  snapshot. The **cached** prefix = stable system prompt + tree context block; the per-turn user
  message goes last. Streamed replies rendered progressively via Turbo Streams over
  ActionCable (`AdvisorReplyJob` broadcasts deltas). Photo attachments per message (styling
  critique: "where should the front be? which branches would you remove?"). The assistant can
  return **proposed actions** (structured: create task / log event) shown as buttons the user
  must confirm — it never writes on its own. Conversation history is kept append-only
  (compaction not needed at expected lengths; cap at N turns with a "start new conversation"
  prompt). **Species conversations**: "Ask the advisor about this species" on the species page
  starts a conversation with species + the user's garden climate as context (no tree), in the
  desktop drawer / mobile sheet of design-system §7.28. Proposed actions without a tree only
  navigate (e.g. "Show the Back bench calendar"); they never change data.
- **Acceptance:** streaming works in the system spec with a stubbed stream; a spec proves the
  cache breakpoint sits after the tree context; proposed actions require confirmation.

#### T5.3 — Natural-language quick log
- **Depends on:** T3.3, T2.1
- **Scope:** a single text box on the dashboard/garden page: "fertilised all the maples on bench
  2 and wired the juniper" → structured call with the user's tree roster (id, nickname, species,
  area) in context → proposed `CareEvent`s in a review table (edit/remove rows) → confirm creates
  them. Ambiguities are surfaced ("which juniper? 2 match").
- **Acceptance:** fixture spec for the ambiguous and multi-tree cases; nothing is saved without
  confirmation.

### M6 — Notifications

#### T6.1 — Inbox, email and ntfy
- **Depends on:** T4.2, T4.3
- **Scope:** `Notification` (user, kind, subject polymorphic, read_at) + bell/inbox UI with a
  live count (Turbo Stream). Channels per user preference: **email weekly digest** (Sunday
  evening local time: this week's tasks, windows opening, alerts, trees with no journal entry
  in 60 days), **urgent weather alerts** immediately by email, and optionally **ntfy** (user
  enters topic + server URL; `NtfyNotifier` PORO over Net::HTTP; "send test" button). Quiet hours.
  Mailer previews. Unsubscribe links (signed).
- **Acceptance:** the digest job respects time zones (spec with two users in different zones);
  ntfy request stubbed and asserted; preferences are honoured for each kind × channel.

### M7 — Sharing, QR tags & public profiles

#### T7.1 — Shared gardens
- **Depends on:** T1.1, T0.2
- **Scope:** invite someone to a garden by email with a role (`editor`: full tree/journal/task
  access; `viewer`: read-only). An existing user gets a membership; a new user gets an
  `Invitation` with the membership attached. The authorisation matrix goes through
  `Garden#accessible_by?`, with a request spec per role × action. Journal events show who
  logged them. Leave garden / remove member / transfer ownership. Notifications go to all members
  (respecting preferences).
- **Acceptance:** the role × action matrix spec passes; a viewer can't mutate anything (UI hides
  controls and the server rejects requests).

#### T7.2 — Public tree & garden profiles
- **Depends on:** T3.2
- **Scope:** "Make public" toggle → unguessable `public_slug` URL, read-only page (no auth):
  photo progression timeline + compare slider, species, style, years in training, a curated
  journal subset (styling/repot events only, notes optional per event). Garden showcase page
  lists its public trees. **Never expose location or area names**; `noindex` by default with an
  opt-in. Open Graph meta with the primary photo.
- **Acceptance:** private trees 404 publicly; a spec asserts no coordinates/place names appear
  in the public HTML.

#### T7.3 — QR tree tags
- **Depends on:** T3.5
- **Scope:** `/t/:tag_code` → tree page if signed in with access (else the public page if
  public, else sign-in). `rqrcode` SVG. Printable label sheet (print CSS, selectable trees, label
  sizes for common waterproof label stock) showing the QR code, nickname, species and acquired
  year and tag code. `/t/:tag_code` opens the tree page with the **T3.5 quick-log sheet** already
  open and the "Scanned tag NBR-7F3K" context row (design-system §8.3). Works offline for trees in
  the cached list.
- **Acceptance:** redirect matrix spec; print view renders N labels.

### M8 — Inventory

#### T8.1 — Pots
- **Depends on:** T3.3
- **Scope:** `Pot` CRUD with photo, filters (available, size range, shape). A `repotted` event
  can pick a pot → `PotAssignment` history (the previous pot is freed automatically). Tree page
  shows the current pot and pot history. "Find a pot for this tree": available pots filtered by
  size relative to the tree (a simple rule: length ≈ ⅔ of tree height for upright styles —
  displayed as a suggestion).
- **Acceptance:** the repot flow updates assignments; a pot can't be in use by two trees.

#### T8.2 — Soil, supplies & mixes
- **Depends on:** T8.1
- **Scope:** `SoilComponent`, `SoilMix` (saved recipes; species pages can "save recommended mix"),
  `Supply` with quantities and low-stock flags (the dashboard shows low stock). Repot/fertilise/
  treat event forms and the quick-log sheet can pick a product from inventory, with the hint
  "From inventory · 38 left". When an amount is logged in the product's unit, the stock is
  decremented (and restored if the event is deleted); otherwise the event is linked only.
- **Acceptance:** CRUD specs; low-stock appears on the dashboard.

### M9 — Hardening

#### T9.1 — Export & account deletion
- **Depends on:** M3–M8 as available
- **Scope:** a background job builds a ZIP: JSON (Jbuilder) of gardens, trees, events, tasks,
  assessments, plus CSV of trees/events, plus original photos; emailed download link (expires
  7 days). Account deletion: removes the user's owned gardens (or requires transferring shared
  ones), purges attachments, keeps anonymised `AiRequest` rows for the spend history.
- **Acceptance:** the export round-trip spec checks the JSON contains every tree; deletion leaves
  no orphaned blobs.

#### T9.2 — Ops, admin & quality pass
- **Depends on:** all prior
- **Scope:** admin dashboard: users, invitations, AI spend by feature/month vs budget, species
  queue counts, job failures. Error reporting (Rails 8 `Rails.error` subscriber → log + ntfy to
  the admin). Accessibility pass against UI rules Pattern 9. N+1 audit (`prosopite` or
  `bullet` in dev/test). Fragment caching on tree cards/species pages (Russian-doll with
  `touch: true`). Backup restore drill documented. Security review (`/security-review`).
- **Acceptance:** zero N+1 warnings in the system suite; `brakeman` clean; the restore drill
  has actually been done once.

#### T9.3 — Units honour the user's settings everywhere
- **Depends on:** nothing new; it can run at any point (added 2026-09-30 at the owner's request)
- **Goal:** every temperature, length, distance, weight and volume the app shows follows the
  signed-in user's `temperature_unit` (°C/°F) and `unit_system` (metric/imperial) from
  Settings › Preferences. Storage stays metric and Celsius.
- **Known gap:** the species page (`/species/:slug`) does not fully honour the settings.
- **Scope:**
  - Audit every screen and email for a displayed quantity: species index and page (every profile
    section, the hardiness popover, the care calendar), gardens (climate card, thresholds, weather
    strip), trees (facts, form hints, size classes), and anything added since.
  - For each one, record whether it comes from a structured value (convert it through the shared
    `Temperature` / `format_measure` helpers) or from generated prose that carries a literal unit
    (decide per case: structured value plus template, or render both units).
  - Fix every gap. One conversion path per quantity type; no unit literals in views.
  - Signed-out and public pages (T7.2) use a stated default.
- **Acceptance:** a spec renders each audited screen for a metric/Celsius user and an
  imperial/Fahrenheit user and finds no quantity in the other system; the species page spec covers
  every profile section.

#### T9.4 — Spelling follows the user's language setting
- **Depends on:** nothing new; it can run at any point (added 2026-09-30 at the owner's request)
- **Goal:** each user reads the app in their own English. British English stays (it is what the
  app is written in today: "Fertilise", "Catalogue", "colour"), and a user who chooses American
  English sees "Fertilize", "Catalog", "color" everywhere, the same way units follow their setting.
- **Known gap:** there is no language setting yet. Every user gets British spellings, in
  hand-written copy and in the generated species profiles.
- **Scope:**
  - **The setting:** a per-user language preference in Settings › Preferences (British English,
    American English), with a default for new users and for signed-out pages (§9).
  - **UI copy:** move views, helper constants, flash messages, emails, validation messages and
    enum labels (care types such as "fertilise") to I18n with `en-GB` and `en-US` locales, set per
    request from the user's preference.
  - **Generated content:** species profiles are one shared catalogue written in one spelling.
    Decide how a profile reaches a user in their spelling (§9): a spelling transform at render, a
    stored variant per locale, or generation per locale. Later AI surfaces that answer one user
    (diagnosis, advisor) are prompted in that user's language.
  - Stored keys and schema field names stay as they are.
  - A guard spec: the `en-US` locale and an American user's pages contain no word from a
    British-spelling list, and the reverse for `en-GB`. Code comments and `docs/` are out of scope.
- **Acceptance:** a spec renders the main screens (home, species index and page, tree page, photos,
  settings) for a British and an American user and finds no spelling from the other list; changing
  the setting changes the next page.

#### T9.5 — Infinite scroll for paginated lists
- **Depends on:** nothing new; it can run at any point (added 2026-10-06 at the owner's request)
- **Goal:** every paginated list loads its next page as the reader scrolls, instead of making them
  tap Previous / Next.
- **Known gap:** `/trees` and `/species` page with pagy and a Previous / Next pager inside their
  Turbo Frame (`trees/_pager`, `species/_pager`). The Journal tab pages by 30 days with an "older"
  link. The photo page's Newer / Older steps between photos and isn't a list, so it stays as is.
- **Scope:**
  - Audit every paginated list, including anything added since (admin reviews, the garden-wide
    journal, tasks).
  - Use one shared pattern for all of them: a lazy `turbo-frame` "next page" sentinel
    (`loading: :lazy`) that appends the next page's rows and its own next sentinel, or Turbo
    Stream appends. No new gem. Filters, sorts and chips in the URL keep working, and changing a
    filter starts again at the first page.
  - Keep a plain link as the fallback (no JavaScript, keyboard, and screen readers) and announce
    the loaded rows in an `aria-live` region. Show a loading state and an end-of-list state.
    Scroll position and Back keep working.
  - The loaded pages stay usable at 390 px with no layout jump, and a long session doesn't slow
    down (decide whether to cap the rows kept on the page).
- **Acceptance:** a system spec per list scrolls to the end and sees every record exactly once,
  with no Previous / Next pager. A filter change resets to page one. The fallback link works with
  JavaScript off. Axe stays clean in both themes.

#### T9.6 — Tree page tabs keep the scroll position
- **Depends on:** nothing new; it can run at any point (added 2026-10-06 at the owner's request)
- **Goal:** choosing a tab on the tree page (Overview, Photos, Journal and the later tabs) keeps the
  reader where they are, so the tab bar and the newly active tab stay in view.
- **Known gap:** each tab is its own page (`/trees/:id`, `/trees/:id/photos`, `/trees/:id/journal`),
  so choosing one is a Turbo Drive visit that scrolls to the top. On a phone the hero pushes the
  tab bar below the fold, and the reader has to scroll down again to see which tab is active.
- **Scope:**
  - Keep the scroll position when moving between a tree's tabs. Choose the mechanism when planning
    (for example a Turbo Frame around the tab bar and panel that advances the URL, a morphing
    visit with scroll preservation, or restoring the offset after the visit). The URL per tab,
    Back/Forward and a direct visit keep working.
  - Only tab changes keep the position. Arriving on a tree page from anywhere else still starts at
    the top. If the new tab's content is shorter than the current offset, the tab bar stays
    visible.
  - Focus stays on the chosen tab and the change is announced as it is today.
- **Acceptance:** a system spec at 390 px scrolls the tree page until the tab bar is in view,
  chooses each tab in turn and finds the tab bar still in the viewport with the chosen tab marked
  current. Back returns to the previous tab. A visit from `/trees` starts at the top.

## 10. Definition of done (every task)

- RSpec green; new behaviour covered by model and request specs, plus system specs for key flows.
- No live HTTP in the test suite; AI and weather fixtures are committed.
- `.claude/rules` respected: no service objects, strict locals, no ERB assignment or logic,
  `docs/design-system.md` followed (components + tokens, no hard-coded colours, every state,
  both themes, 390 px width), inline errors, HTML5 input attributes, empty states, loading states.
- rubocop + brakeman clean; CI green.
- `docs/decisions.md` updated when a task makes a decision this plan didn't.
